notes: Topline: enterprise procurement driven by low-latency trading assistant use — SLA is critical.
POC summary: 2-week bench run completed 2026-02-25. Redwood delivered dedicated cluster prototype; measured sustained throughput and failover behavior.
Throughput/Reserved GPU ask (Halo): baseline 8x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, burst up to 16x for market open/close windows; predictable capacity during US/EU trading hours.
Redwood proposed config: 10 reserved GPUs with autoscale headroom to 16 for 30-minute bursts; suggested cron-based scaling tied to market hours.
Throughput guarantees discussed: sustain 150k tokens/min (approx. 2.5k reqs/min @200 tokens) with 5% degradation allowance during bursts.

Latency SLOs (negotiation points): Halo requires p95 < 200ms for <512-token requests during baseline load and p99 < 800ms. Redwood's default p95 was 120-180ms in bench; p99 spikes to ~700ms under load — acceptable if credits attached.
Uptime target: Halo asking for 99.99% for dedicated pool (financial SLA). Redwood counters with 99.95% (standard) + escalated credits for 99.9-99.95 tier. Key negotiation item.
Credit schedule under discussion: tiered service credits tied to monthly uptime (examples on table):
- >=99.95%: 0% credits (standard full service)
- 99.90–99.95%: 10% service credit
- 99.00–99.90%: 25% service credit
- <99.00%: 50% service credit + optional termination right after two consecutive months
Halo requests a steeper credit curve and a one-time reimbursement for measurable trading losses for outages >2 hours during market hours — Redwood legal pushing back on explicit financial indemnity.

Maintenance windows: Redwood proposes monthly maintenance windows (up to 4 hours) scheduled Sundays 02:00–06:00 ET. Halo needs maintenance outside US/EU market overlap; wants rare allowed windows and advance 30-day notice for major updates.

Support & response times: Halo demands P1 response <= 30 minutes and on-call escalation for production impact; Redwood standard is P1 response <= 1 hour. P2/P3 discussed: 4 hours / 24 hours. Also require on-site remote warroom during cutovers for first month.
Operational controls asked: runbooks, playbooks, post-incident reports within 48 hours, access to traceroute/traces and token-level logging for debug (redacted for PII).
Security/compliance notes: SOC2 report shared 2026-02-27; Halo's security team still needs ISO27001 evidence and KMS integration details for key rotation policy.

Cost sensitivity: club-level ARR targets mean Halo wants committed discount for reserved capacity and a CPI (cost per inference) cap. Redwood offered tiered committed discount + credits for failed SLAs.
Fallback/routing: requirement to failover to Redwood hosted (lower priority) model variants in multi-region fallback; must not leak order execution metadata — RBAC and VPC peering checklist pending.
Legal notes: Halo legal flagged 'force majeure' language and wants more explicit language around maintenance-related uptime exclusion and notice periods.
Quote/POC artifacts: attach benchmark PDF + bench logs in Drive; SE to produce latency percentile heatmaps for next call.
Halo quote expectation: final commercial terms (including SLA appendix) by 2026-05 to align with budget cycle.
Sales tactic: propose 90-day pilot with credits and limited indemnity, followed by full reserved contract after success metrics hit (SLO compliance for 2 consecutive months).
Direct quote from CTO (initial call): 'We need absolute clarity on what happens during a slow cluster — trading signals can't wait 30 minutes.'
Action items: SE to provide revised SLA appendix with proposed credit table, Redwood legal to draft compromise maintenance clause, finance to model committed discount vs usage-based overlay.
